We use it primarily in the context of a code reviewer, and it occasionally finds subtle security/workflow/backwards-compat issues that Claude and GPT do not. Claude makes final judgments on whether the findings are material and how they should be fixed.

Argon also tends to write particularly warm copy and external messages - unsurprising with Google's particular access to email data and caches of writing from the early internet.

We haven't really used it to write code from scratch - generally, we're wary of these exact things, and feel like Claude continues to have good enough architectural instincts that we've doubled down into the Claude ecosystem, with mods and tooling (including this multi-agent reviewer) that accelerate our workflows.

Are you sure about Argon? My experience has been it seems to understand code but it completely destroyed a couple of projects I was working on. Others like Theo used it to work on T3 Code and said it benchmaxxed and was atrocious.

Our team figured out the only stable way to do this was to either use OpenRouter for API, or for subscriptions, to get Ultra Gemini accounts on personal Gmail accounts (no way to do this for individual members of an org without upgrading the entire org!) and hook those to the Antigravity CLI which Claude Code can then orchestrate for second opinions.

children.text:
To my understanding it has nothing to do with output and entirely to do with the understanding of the input together as basically one input stream. An LLM with a vision encoder or audio encoder takes the media and turns them into tokens the LLM reads and then turns into its text latents (basically).

It’s like the difference between me looking at a picture, describing it to you, and then you trying to form that picture in your mind. You might get close, but it will never be the picture I’m looking at. If I then ask you questions about the picture, you can’t answer any questions about any details that I didn’t describe. I believe that is exactly the information and understanding loss that an Omni model attempts to address, which doesn’t have anything to do with output.

Some models do also offer “Omni” output, but that is more like a feature of the model than what Omni models are by design I think.
The "omni" naming for a video-only model is so confusing. I was under the impression omni referred to models that can output text and audio too.
